Reliability and Long-Term Course of Itch-Scratch Severity in Atopic Dermatitis (AD)
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the longitudinal course of excoriations was heterogeneous, with 30.6 and 5.4% of adults with moderate and severe excoriations at baseline.
we have shown that itch and scratching are not static in patients with AD, that they fluctuate over time, and that they are associated with the disease activity.
itch/scratch severity in AD is a valid measure of the burden of itch in adults with AD and that it is associated with other AD measures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scratching/excoriations are a common and burdensome symptom of AD.
the severity of scratching and excoriation in AD patients is not a static condition.
there is substantial heterogeneity in the longitudinal course of excoriations in AD.
